Research problem and state of practice The optimisation object is a model update in weight space, not the individual A/B factor coordinates. Two different factorisations can encode the same delta; naive averaging destroys invariance. Variable-rank clients make the representation problem harder. A candidate protocol may aggregate reconstructed deltas, concatenate rank factors or compress the result to a selected rank with an explicit approximation budget. This subject has established prior art. A promising idea becomes a research contribution only when it names a competing baseline, controls the evaluation budget, demonstrates a reproducible improvement or reports a valid negative result. Keep paper claims distinct from independently replicated observations. Worked research design Independent baseline: sample-weighted full delta aggregation. Compare with factor averaging on the scalar A1=B1=1, A2=B2=−1 case; the correct delta average is 1 whereas factor average yields 0. Extend to random matrices with testable Frobenius error. Falsifiable hypothesis and measurements Hypothesis: controlled rank-aware compression reduces transmitted bytes at a fixed non-inferiority bound on held-out loss. Retune all methods under matched update-communication and compute budgets, and report failed configurations. Collect an immutable dataset/checkpoint identifier, compiler/backend version, model shape, worker topology, bandwidth and RTT, random seeds, held-out evaluation, communication bytes, total time and verified cost. Pre-register the main success metric before comparing implementations; report confidence ranges if observed effects are small. Integration boundary Use existing Framework training, optimisation, model-provenance, messaging and lifecycle APIs. Where a new capability is required, develop a bounded native C23 component and qualify it against a simple independent numerical oracle. Do not place unreviewed learner code directly in the production Bank/TMS services, and do not claim networked training or cryptographic proof from an in-process demonstration. Questions for a research notebook Which property of the method is genuinely novel relative to the strongest listed baseline? Which hardware, dataset or adversary assumption could reverse the outcome? What failed experiment would disprove the proposed advantage? How could a different research group reproduce every measured result? Primary literature LoRA — Low-Rank Adaptation, Hu et al. Research problem and state of practice MoE activates only a subset of experts for each token, but expert routing can require many cross-device dispatches. On a slow wide-area network, the inter-expert communication path may dominate. A decentralized MoE experiment should separate model sparsity from network transfer and include failure handling for missing experts. Contrast with state-space mixers whose recurrence changes memory/communication patterns. This subject has established prior art. A promising idea becomes a research contribution only when it names a competing baseline, controls the evaluation budget, demonstrates a reproducible improvement or reports a valid negative result. Keep paper claims distinct from independently replicated observations. Worked research design Suppose an expert dispatch transfers 8 KiB each direction for 100 tokens: 1.6 MiB of round-trip payload before metadata. At 10 Mbps, serialization alone exceeds one second; add RTT and the cost can dominate a small model. This is an illustrative bound, not measured MoE latency. Falsifiable hypothesis and measurements Hypothesis: local expert placement with bounded fallback reduces WAN bytes per successfully processed token compared with naive round-robin expert placement while retaining a quality threshold. Learning path Canonical Markdown NextWhat you will learnExplain evaluate cryptographic commitments against independent signatures with explicit assumptions, an independently checkable worked example and the limits of the evidence. Concept and mechanismHypothesis: independent authenticated anchors improve detection of rewritten research receipts compared with a local chain whose expected tip is stored in the same mutable database. Evaluate attack detection at equal event rate and message overhead. The hash digest binds bytes; the signer or trusted process binds authority. Keep the experiment’s adversary model explicit. Worked exampleFor each accepted round, compare locally stored root R and an independently signed copy of R. A simulated attacker rewrites local history and recomputes a fresh root; the external signed anchor remains unchanged. Try it yourselfSpecify a falsification case and test data containing benign corrections and hostile rewrites.Reveal the fully worked answerThe hypothesis fails to add value if independent anchoring introduces no demonstrable detection or governance improvement over the baseline. Where the proof stopsA signed anchor does not prove honest gradient computation.A native test can verify byte-level membership but cannot by itself authenticate a participant, authorise financial transactions, establish consensus or prove neural model improvement. Record the independent root, protocol and unperformed tests. Native implementation boundaryUse the existing Umicom Framework C23 SHA-256 and ordered record chain. The opt-in Merkle service consumes validated digests and exposes bounded membership checks. Existing Python and PowerShell teaching tools remain alternatives, not the implementation. Learning path Canonical Markdown NextWhat you will learnExplain build a merkle tree from transaction digests with explicit assumptions, an independently checkable worked example and the limits of the evidence. Concept and mechanismAn ordered group of transactions can be represented by a single root digest. Hash each transaction into a leaf node, combine neighbouring nodes into parents, and repeat until one digest remains. Real blockchains specify their own precise byte encodings; the Umicom learning algorithm uses domain-separated SHA-256 on already-hashed record digests. A Merkle root is an authenticated-data-structure commitment only when obtained from a trusted block/header/anchor. Worked exampleFor transactions A,B,C,D, compute four leaf-domain hashes, then parents P0=H(nodeDomain||LA||LB), P1=H(nodeDomain||LC||LD), and bind the top with count four. Try it yourselfDraw the exact path from transaction C to the final root and identify the sibling digest at each level.Reveal the fully worked answerC needs sibling D at its leaf level and sibling P0 at the next level; the final count-bound digest is computed after combining. Where the proof stopsBitcoin, Ethereum and this native educational implementation do not share identical tree encodings.A native test can verify byte-level membership but cannot by itself authenticate a participant, authorise financial transactions, establish consensus or prove neural model improvement. Record the independent root, protocol and unperformed tests. Native implementation boundaryUse the existing Umicom Framework C23 SHA-256 and ordered record chain. The opt-in Merkle service consumes validated digests and exposes bounded membership checks. Existing Python and PowerShell teaching tools remain alternatives, not the implementation. Learning path Canonical Markdown Previous NextWhat you will learnExplain understand byzantine faults, equivocation and quorum intersection with explicit assumptions, an independently checkable worked example and the limits of the evidence. Concept and mechanismA Byzantine participant may send contradictory statements to different peers rather than merely crash. Classical BFT protocols address such behaviour with authenticated messages, quorum intersection and view-change rules. An often-studied model uses 3f+1 replicas and 2f+1 commit votes for f Byzantine faults. Real protocols differ, and the number alone is not a complete algorithm. Worked exampleWith f=1 the classical configuration has 4 replicas and a 3-vote quorum. Two size-three groups overlap in at least two replicas, so at least one overlapping member is honest if no more than one is faulty. Course routeCanonical MarkdownPrevious HTML lessonNext HTML lessonBits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Level: Beginner–intermediate · Prerequisites: Distributed Learning Lessons 001–012. Learning objective Describe bind one worker to one training round in your own words and work through a small numerical or lifecycle experiment. Understand the idea A learning worker receives a specific model version, shard and task. A local ticket records the assignment’s lifetime, whereas an authenticated remote identity requires separate cryptography. Keeping the two separate makes it possible to cancel a task without pretending to revoke someone’s public key. Three notions must always stay distinct: training changes model parameters, coordination decides which work may proceed, and verification evaluates what evidence can be trusted. A blockchain may eventually record decisions, but neither transactions nor hashes replace backpropagation. Classroom walkthrough Imagine a student given worksheet 7. Returning the answer to worksheet 6 is not acceptable just because the student is registered. Similarly a correct-shaped delta labelled with the wrong base checkpoint must be refused. Practical native C23 connection The existing Umicom Framework owns training arithmetic and its new federated-job interface accounts for local assignments. The distributed-learning laboratory links the real Framework interfaces; no Python trainer is added to Umicom. All examples use synthetic IDs and synthetic deltas. Real training, signed network messages and end-to-end quality certification are separate research stages. Exercise Question: Write three identifiers that belong in a worker assignment. Show the explained answer Worker identity, shared base-checkpoint identity and authorised dataset-shard identity; include a unique round or job identifier. Suggested demonstration Sketch the lifecycle: propose → inspect permission → admit → local work → submit → independently check → aggregate → evaluate. Mark where it is appropriate to refuse a task and where a failure must leave model weights unchanged. Write one example of a negative result worth reporting. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation · Sammy Hegab Learning objectives Configure an optional native Umicom Framework learning project, interpret its output and understand where ordinary shell commands stop and Framework functionality begins. 1. Locate the native implementation The implementation is Framework-owned: framework/src/ai/training/decoder_projection_adapter.c contains the adapter's owned tape and checkpoints; framework/src/ai/training/supervised_continuation.c tracks deterministic training order and serialises the combined state; framework/src/ai/training/supervised_quality.c checks quality thresholds. The educational demonstration itself is framework/learning/native-ai-resumable/continuation_demo.c. It passes wholly synthetic teaching examples to existing source-admission and dataset services. It is not a second trainer. 2. Configure in PowerShell Set-Location 'C:\umicom\Umicom-Applications' $env:Path = 'C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin;' + $env:Path cmake -S '.\framework\learning\native-ai-resumable' ` -B '.\build\windows-ucrt64-ai-resume-debug' -G Ninja ` -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER='C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\gcc.exe' ` -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Configure failed' } cmake --build '.\build\windows-ucrt64-ai-resume-debug' --parallel 2 if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Build failed' } ctest --test-dir '.\build\windows-ucrt64-ai-resume-debug' ` -R '^framework\.ai\.(continuation|supervised|adaptation)\.' ` --output-on-failure --no-tests=error if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Regression failed' } The build should compile the original Framework tensor and decoder services together with the additive checkpoint/continuation module. Do not call this successful until your configured checkout reports passing tests. 3. Follow the demo data flow The demonstration creates its own fictional public learning sources, validates the source-review evidence, constructs a small dataset and creates a frozen decoder plus two selected low-rank projection adapters. It trains one approved example, exports its combined adapter and cursor snapshot, destroys the original adapter and restores a newly owned adapter. It then completes the remaining epochs and reports aggregate held-out losses. It does not write a checkpoint file to a fixed path or load arbitrary internet models. Applications that need durable snapshots use approved Framework storage and identity controls. 4. Check the three key results Observe the restored cursor and completed steps. Confirm the final steps match the number of training examples multiplied by completed epochs. Confirm that the frozen decoder checkpoint remains unchanged. Finally, compare independent resumed and uninterrupted runs in the CTest regression: their final snapshot bytes must match on the same build. A runnable native demonstration is not proof of a useful general-purpose language model. The current teaching decoder is intentionally small and bounded. The goal here is correct training ownership, deterministic state and honest evaluation evidence. Practice Question: Why don't we copy the Transformer mathematics into the educational CLI? Answer: The Framework is the single numerical authority. The CLI constructs synthetic inputs, calls published Framework APIs and presents results, making the same components reusable in Studio and later Umicom AI applications. Continue with preparing real authorised sources. Service to Many Leads to Greatness. Educational C23 examples; not a production financial or model-training certification. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation · Sammy Hegab Learning objectives Draw a source-to-dataset pipeline that respects permissions, original asset identity, train/evaluation separation and privacy. Learn why text extraction and model training must remain different stages. 1. Original assets are not yet training data A PDF, DOCX document, source-code file, audio recording, video or image contains material in its original format. A training system cannot responsibly treat every byte as an approved text example. It first needs an appropriate Framework-owned extractor or provider adapter, a record of the asset's origin and licence, and an explicit human review of the prepared derivative. For videos with trusted subtitles, the existing Framework Creative Workspace can parse supported SRT and WebVTT subsets into validated caption tracks. The existing native caption-to-text service can prepare reviewable text from such a track. This is not speech recognition; footage without approved transcripts needs a separately qualified extraction provider. For PDF, DOCX and image data, use an already available Framework document/media component where supported and add native C23 provider boundaries when a required format is missing. Never silently assume all binary or scanned documents can be decoded by the current teaching dataset loader. 2. Record both hashes The original asset SHA-256 identifies the reviewed input bytes. The prepared derivative SHA-256 identifies the exact reviewed UTF-8 text bytes. If a video is captioned twice or one document is split into multiple examples, both derivatives should retain the same original asset identity. The Framework's reviewed-source admission and ReviewedCorpusAudit make those identities available for a source-level train/evaluation separation. A paraphrased duplicate or nearly identical recording still requires a separate near-duplicate review; exact hashes cannot detect semantic duplication. 3. Keep model-facing text separate from provenance A reviewed prompt/completion JSONL row contains just the approved training prompt and response. Its evidence record separately holds hashes, source grouping, partition and reviewed span positions. This design reduces the risk that a model learns filenames, personal identifiers or editorial metadata merely because those values were packaged alongside the text. It does not provide automatic personal-data redaction, licence discovery or proof of the right to train. Those decisions must be separately established before import. Restricted or private assets must never be admitted into a public example repository to make demonstration output convenient. 4. Move from an approved row to a training window The Framework byte tokenizer represents raw bytes as token IDs offset by four, reserving IDs for PAD, BOS, EOS and UNK. The supervised-window component builds [BOS]+prompt+completion+[EOS], creates next-token targets and masks prompt/padding targets. Only assistant-response bytes and EOS contribute to the selected-token cross-entropy. No document extraction logic belongs in Bits2Banking. Educational pages can explain the workflow, while the actual C23 operations remain reusable Framework services. Practice A video produces two corrected subtitle documents. Should its transcripts automatically go to different evaluation partitions? No. Both share the original video identity and must retain the same source-level partition to reduce leakage. Continue with quality gates. Service to Many Leads to Greatness. Educational C23 examples; not a production financial or model-training certification. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation · Sammy Hegab Learning objectives Distinguish numerical test evidence, quality decisions, source authenticity and model promotion. Explain why no single successful number authorises an AI component to control banking or trading operations. 1. Which question is each test answering? A successful native build confirms the compiler accepted the source and linkage. A gradient regression confirms the tested backward calculation agrees with its reference. A checkpoint round-trip confirms the selected adapter weights were restored as intended. A held-out evaluation measures prediction error on examples isolated from training by source identity. None of these tests alone proves that a model gives correct, lawful, secure or useful responses in unfamiliar situations. A small experimental decoder should remain a laboratory even if its numerical loss falls consistently. 2. Require a comparison against a fixed baseline For two observations from the same held-out dataset, define lossChange = afterLoss − beforeLoss and accuracyChange = afterAccuracy − beforeAccuracy. Negative loss change is usually favourable. Positive accuracy change means more exact next-token matches. Different evaluation populations cannot be compared by these formulas without further statistical controls. The Framework's UmiAiTrainingSupervisedQualityEvaluate receives two verified evaluation summaries and explicit tolerances. It can report accepted=0 while returning UMI_STATUS_OK because a legitimate quality failure is a finding, not a parser or memory error. 3. Treat quality and trust as different gates A snapshot's unkeyed SHA-256 protects against accidental corruption and binds model/data identifiers. It is not a publisher signature. The existing Framework model release, trust and approval services must remain separate authorities. Human review and access-control restrictions must also apply to training sources and downstream application actions. For Umicom Studio's assistant, initial integration might present suggestions for a developer to review and test. Generated code should not be executed silently. In Umicom Bank or Trader, core transaction validation, pricing, risk, ledger consistency, identity and authorisations must remain independent of any experimental LLM response. 4. Build a sensible evidence record Record the frozen model SHA-256, ordered approved-corpus SHA-256, exact adapter snapshot digest, declared training policy, completed SGD step count, compiler and environment. Record held-out loss and accuracy with the evaluated token counts. Keep privacy-sensitive source content in its authorised storage, not in a public evidence log. A future production model additionally needs independent domain benchmarks, adverse-case evaluation, resource limits, monitoring, rollback planning and approved release procedures. There is no shortcut from one low loss to enterprise approval. Practice A candidate reduces cross-entropy but fails a mandatory held-out accuracy threshold. Should it be automatically promoted? No. The quality gate is not fully satisfied, and the release authority is separate even when it is. An automatic production upgrade without the necessary controls would exceed the evidence. Revisit replay verification and source review. Service to Many Leads to Greatness. Educational C23 examples; not a production financial or model-training certification. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering The engineering question A Transformer block is not an entire language model. One block takes a matrix of token representations and returns a matrix of the same width. A stack sends that output into the next block. The Umicom Framework already owns the pre-layer-normalised block, so the correct next step is to compose several copies, not to write a second attention implementation. For an input X of shape [T, C], the first block returns H1 = Block1(X) and the second returns H2 = Block2(H1). T is the number of token positions; C is the feature width. The blocks share an architecture but have different trainable weights. A token embedding table and a position embedding table produce the initial X; an output projection maps the final hidden state to vocabulary logits. Follow the Framework implementation The new UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderCreate owns a training tape and the parameter leaves for every layer. UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderLogits performs one full-context forward evaluation. Each layer calls the already established UmiAiTrainingTransformerBlockForward, with the exact public parameter order. Applications use this Framework API; they do not calculate attention or maintain model tensors themselves. #include "umicom/ai/training/stacked_decoder.h" UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderConfig config = { 16U, 4U, 8U, 12U, 2U, 2U, UINT64_C(20261026) }; UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoder *model = NULL; UmiStatus status = UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderCreate(&config, &model); /* Inspect status before using model; destroy it once when finished. */ Here the model has vocabulary 16, four positions, eight features, 12 feed-forward features, two attention heads and two distinct Transformer blocks. It remains deliberately small enough to inspect. What this does not provide The old single-block checkpoint is not a stacked checkpoint. The stacked model is a separately identified family. It still uses learned absolute positions, FP32 tape arithmetic and a complete context forward pass. It is neither a modern GPU-scale model nor proof of useful prose generation. Practice Draw the operations from token IDs through two blocks to logits. Which components are shared implementations, and which parameters must be independent? Worked answer Token IDs → token embeddings + learned position embeddings → Block 1 → Block 2 → logits projection. The same Framework operators implement both blocks, but their Q/K/V, normalisation and feed-forward parameter values are separate. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering Shapes are the first correctness test Most neural numerical bugs are dimension errors or unintended broadcasting. A layer stack requires each block to preserve the hidden width. In a single-sequence educational example, start with four tokens, eight channels, and two attention heads. The input and output of every block are [4,8]. Each head processes 8/2 = 4 channels. A 12-feature feed-forward sublayer first expands [4,8] to [4,12], then contracts it back to [4,8]. A learned token table for a 16-token vocabulary has shape [16,8], and a learned position table for four positions has shape [4,8]. The vocabulary projection has shape [8,16]. Consequently the logits are [4,16]—64 scores, not 64 probabilities. Inspect before allocating UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderPlan delegates parameter and memory arithmetic to UmiAiTrainingModelScalingEstimateBuild, the existing Framework scaling service. The stacked model additionally validates the live tape's conservative tensor/context/layer bounds. A candidate may fit a theoretical memory estimate yet exceed a concrete tensor or computational-graph capacity. Tensor Shape Why Token embeddings [16,8] 16 IDs, each mapped to 8 numbers Block Q/K/V projection [8,8] Hidden width is unchanged Feed-forward up [8,12] Expand features Feed-forward down [12,8] Restore hidden width Final logits [4,16] One score per token and vocabulary ID The current model has one sequence per call. Extending to independent sequences requires explicit sequence masks and validated attention isolation; concatenating unrelated documents as one causal stream changes the training problem. Practice For context length six, channels twelve, three attention heads and hidden width twenty-four, calculate the head width and final logits shape for vocabulary size 200. Worked answer Head width is 12/3 = 4 channels. With six token positions and 200 possible next-token IDs, logits have shape [6,200], containing 1,200 floating-point values. Verify that the actual Framework implementation admits the shape; mathematical validity alone does not guarantee implementation capacity. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering One random seed, many independently owned weights An educational Transformer should give repeatable experiments. The existing Framework provides UmiAiTrainingRandomSeed and UmiAiTrainingRandomFillUniform. The stacked constructor advances this one caller-owned RNG state as it creates every parameter tensor in a defined order. This makes two fresh models with the same configuration and seed produce the same initial logits on a qualifying build. Every layer owns separate attention matrices, layer-normalisation scales/biases, and feed-forward matrices/biases. Normalisation scales begin at 1; ordinary biases begin at 0; dense projections and embedding tables receive seeded finite initial values. These are transparent laboratory initialisation rules, not a claim that this scheme is optimal for billion-parameter training. Why independent weights matter If all six layers accidentally referenced one set of weights, the resulting system would repeatedly apply the same transformation rather than a stack of independently parameterised blocks. In some model families intentional sharing is possible, but that is a different architecture and must be declared, trained and checkpointed explicitly. The constructor uses the tape's UmiAiTrainingTensorCreate for every leaf, so ownership is clear. On an allocation or validation failure, it destroys the partially constructed tape and leaves the caller's model pointer unchanged. Check it yourself Create two models with identical settings, call UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderLogits on the same full context, and compare all logits. Then create a model with a different seed or layer count and compare again. Changing a seed should change initialisation; changing layer count changes the architecture, so numeric parity is not expected. Practice Why is reproducing the same seed insufficient for exact continuation after 100 SGD updates? Worked answer The seed recreates initial weights only. Training changes the weight values; continuation needs the actual updated parameters, training-step identity and the original sequence of data/update choices. For AdamW, moments are also necessary. A seed is not a replacement for a checkpoint. Native stacked Transformer reading path · Mathematics for AI This HTML page accompanies the original editable Markdown manuscript. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering A future token must not affect an earlier logit A decoder-only language model predicts from left to right. The causal mask prevents an earlier token position from attending to a later position. But verifying the mask in one attention head is not sufficient: a composition error could reintroduce future information through another layer, residual connection or wrongly indexed representation. Consider two four-token contexts: [A,B,C,D] and [A,B,X,Y]. They share the first two tokens. For a correctly implemented causal decoder, the logits at positions 0 and 1 must agree within the justified numerical tolerance. The logits at later positions may differ. The new Framework regression executes a real three-layer stack twice with those two contexts. It compares all vocabulary logits for the shared earlier positions. This establishes an observable model-level causality property, not merely a unit test of an isolated attention mask. Why this property survives composition By induction: embeddings at position t use only token t and the position index. If every block's output at t depends only on inputs at positions <=t, then a second block cannot introduce a dependency on >t. Residual addition and per-row normalisation preserve that restriction when implemented over the correct row boundaries. There is a caveat: concatenating unrelated documents without resetting the sequence boundary makes earlier text from the previous document visible. A triangular causal mask alone does not implement document isolation. Practice Which rows must match for [M,N,P,Q] versus [M,N,R,S]? Why does comparing only the next chosen token miss some mistakes? Worked answer Rows 0 and 1 should have matching logits for every vocabulary ID. Two incorrect logit distributions might still choose the same highest-scoring token, so token-ID equality alone is weaker than full-logit comparison. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering One loss, gradients through the whole stack Training works only if an error at the final vocabulary head can influence earlier learnable weights. Write the forward path as H1 = Block1(X), H2 = Block2(H1), and L = Loss(Logits(H2), targets). The backward pass traverses these dependencies in reverse. It must differentiate the vocabulary projection, Block 2, Block 1, position/token embeddings, and all parameters that contributed to the selected outputs. The stacked model does not implement a second differentiation algorithm. It uses the existing UmiAiTrainingBackward, then updates all trainable leaves in one UmiAiTrainingSgdStepMany transaction. This is full-model educational SGD, not adapter-only fine-tuning. The selected-token loss is the Framework's existing UmiAiTrainingSelectedCrossEntropy composition. Updating safely A train step performs forward computation, selected loss, backwards differentiation and transactional parameter update. Then it rolls the transient graph back to the retained parameter prefix. The weights persist; old intermediate activations do not. A failed candidate SGD transaction must not leave a partially updated layer. The returned loss describes before-update cross-entropy. To measure the new model, call the evaluation API again after the update. A single training example may improve while a held-out example worsens; neither outcome should be concealed. Practical use UmiAiTrainingStackedStep step = {0}; UmiStatus status = UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderTrainSelected( model, inputs, targets, lossMask, contextLength, 0.025F, &step); The caller owns the token arrays and mask; model owns every tensor and optimiser write. Do not mutate the model concurrently from a user interface or background worker. Practice If the model has 27 trainable tensors, should the application perform 27 independent weight updates? Why not? Worked answer No. Pass all parameter handles to the Framework's existing transactional multi-parameter updater. It validates the complete candidate update before changing weights. Independently applying updates can leave an inconsistent partial model if a later parameter fails. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering Prompt context is different from an answer target An assistant receives instructions and surrounding text, then produces a response. During supervised fine-tuning we often want the prompt to condition the response without treating every prompt token as an answer the model should imitate. The existing Framework UmiAiTrainingSupervisedByteWindowBuild prepares fixed-width input IDs, next-token targets and a zero/one loss mask. UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderTrainSelected accepts those arrays and delegates row selection and cross-entropy to UmiAiTrainingSelectedCrossEntropy. In the loss, a selected row contributes one negative log-probability of the correct next token. Mask-zero rows do not contribute direct loss. Selected rows can still backpropagate through earlier prompt-token representations because the response is conditioned on those tokens. A four-position example For a one-byte prompt Q and a one-byte answer A, a complete stream is [BOS, Q, A, EOS]. The teaching window uses the first three items as inputs, the next three as targets, and right-pads to a four-token context. The mask is [0, 1, 1, 0]: predicting the answer and EOS is supervised, while prompt imitation and padding are ignored. Provenance remains mandatory Masking does not grant permission to train. A real document or caption must pass the existing Umicom rights/privacy review and source-hash checks. The current native byte tokenizer preserves UTF-8 bytes but does not provide subword vocabulary, conversation role semantics or automated PII removal. Practice A context has six positions with loss mask [0,0,1,1,1,0]. How many targets contribute to the mean loss? Does a mask-zero prompt position necessarily receive zero gradient everywhere? Worked answer Three targets contribute to the mean. A prompt position contributes no direct cross-entropy row loss, but its representation can influence later selected response rows through causal attention and can therefore receive indirect gradients. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering Parameter bytes are not the whole memory budget Adding Transformer layers increases both parameters and intermediate activations. During a training pass, the Framework tape may retain projected Q/K/V values, attention probabilities, layer-normalisation work, residuals and gradient buffers. Merely multiplying parameter count by four bytes understates actual training-memory requirements. The native stack exposes UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderMemoryInspect, delegating to the canonical tape's memory-accounting service. The report describes tape-owned allocations—not Windows Task Manager RSS, graphics memory, allocator metadata or temporary operator scratch space. What a healthy repeated experiment looks like Take an inspection immediately after creating the model. Repeat a forward evaluation, selected-loss evaluation and a training step. After each operation the graph must be rolled back to its retained leaf prefix. The expected current tensor count and tracked current bytes return to the baseline; peak bytes preserve the highest observed allocation. UmiAiTrainingTapeMemory before = {0}, after = {0}; UmiStatus status = UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderMemoryInspect(model, &before); /* Execute one approved training step and check its result. */ status = UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderMemoryInspect(model, &after); Always check each status before reading the report. A stable tracked allocation does not prove all memory is safe: repeat under sanitizers and investigate application-owned buffers separately. Why the bound is conservative The model uses the existing educational tape, which limits tensor elements and computational-graph nodes. A proposed 40-layer architecture cannot be admitted merely because a spreadsheet estimates affordable parameter memory. Production scaling requires different allocation, activation, optimizer and accelerator strategies. Practice Initial current storage is 7,000 bytes. A forward reaches 11,000, then rewind returns it to 7,000. What should the current and peak readings show? Worked answer Current should return to approximately the original tracked 7,000 bytes if graph lifetime is correct. Peak remains at least 11,000 bytes because it records a historical high-water mark. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering Why this model needs a distinct file identity An existing single-block decoder checkpoint represents one fixed parameter family. A multi-layer model contains more independently ordered weight tensors. Reinterpreting an old checkpoint as a stacked model would silently change the mathematics. The new Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedCheckpointExport creates a separately identified binary record with magic UMISTK01. The format records the model dimensions, seed, completed SGD steps, the number and shapes of parameter tensors and every finite FP32 parameter value. Integers are explicitly little-endian; FP32 bits are copied without depending on a compiler's native C struct packing. A trailing SHA-256 digest covers the encoded bytes before the digest. Export without partial publication Call UmiAiTrainingStackedCheckpointSize to obtain the required byte capacity. Allocate the caller-owned buffer. The export creates a private staging record, validates all tensor values, computes the digest and copies the complete bytes only on success. A short destination retains its previous bytes and write count. The checkpoint is not signed. A content digest detects damage, but someone able to replace the record can calculate a new digest. A trusted publisher and model admission policy are separate Framework security concerns. What is and is not resumable The current stacked trainer uses ordinary stateless SGD. Restoring its weights and completed-step count is enough to resume the same deterministic sequence of SGD operations provided the data, order and learning rate are also unchanged. AdamW additionally needs moment state. The snapshot does not carry experiment dataset approvals or the current position within an epoch. Practice A record has the correct layer count but one weight byte is changed. What does its SHA-256 check tell you? Can it authenticate the person who supplied the record? Worked answer The check should reject the damaged record because the digest no longer matches the content. Even an unmodified matching digest does not authenticate a publisher or prove the checkpoint was trained with authorised data. To continue from update six, save a complete stacked checkpoint after the fifth update. Restoring should recreate the same parameter values and completed-step counter, not recreate the initial model from its seed. The Framework exposes UmiAiTrainingStackedCheckpointInspect and UmiAiTrainingStackedCheckpointDecode. The decoder validates the exact record length, schema, tensor shapes, finite FP32 values and SHA-256 before publishing a newly owned model. The restored model uses the same existing tape and Transformer mathematics as a freshly constructed stack. Prove continuation with two paths Train one model for five steps and save a snapshot. Decode it into an independent second model. Now perform eight more updates on both models, presenting the same token windows in the same order with the same learning rate. Compare all vocabulary logits and the new checkpoint bytes. Under the same build, the expected result is identical for this deterministic stateless-SGD path. A mismatch is actionable. Investigate changed dataset order, missing tensors, an incorrect completed-step field, uninitialised state or floating-point environment differences. Do not widen tolerances to hide a structural error. Important recovery boundary This example proves model-weight continuation in one configuration. Reproducing a complete experiment interrupted mid-epoch additionally needs its dataset identity, shuffle seed, current epoch and next record index. Recovering AdamW requires its first and second moments. No checkpoint should be marked as production-ready without both integrity and independent approval. Practice Model A trains for five steps, is snapshotted, and then takes eight more. What completed-step count should a restored model show after the same eight steps? Worked answer Thirteen updates. The snapshot must preserve five completed steps and the resumed model advances exactly eight more, without counting the restore operation itself as training. Lesson 13 — From a Transformer Block to a Trainable Decoder

← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab · Licence: MIT Level: Progressive native C23 / AI engineering Why training loss is insufficient A decoder can learn to reproduce the small examples it sees repeatedly, yet fail to predict tokens in a different document. This is why the Umicom training workflow separates sources into training and held-out evaluation partitions. The existing Framework admission and reviewed-corpus services are the authority for data-rights approval and source-integrity checks. The new UmiAiTrainingStackedExperimentRun accepts already reviewed caller-owned token windows. It checks model shape, token ranges and selected target masks. It also rejects identical original-source SHA-256 values assigned to both train and evaluation; this prevents one exact original source from leaking across partitions. It does not detect semantic paraphrases or grant training rights. Repeatable epochs A local Framework RNG produces a deterministic permutation of training-example indices for each epoch. Held-out examples are never put in that permutation. The experiment evaluates the held-out partition before training, then after each epoch, recording a token-weighted average loss. A short example with three response targets should have three times the weight of a single-target example when combining average cross-entropies. UmiAiTrainingStackedExperimentReport contains aggregate counts and loss measurements, plus an ordered SHA-256 identity for the supplied token windows. No prompts, customer details or original filenames are emitted. Failure semantics Preflight rejection performs no training. A failure after several updates may leave those valid SGD updates committed; the whole multi-epoch experiment is not automatically transactional. Applications needing all-or-nothing training should snapshot an approved model before running and restore through Framework services upon a reviewed failure. Practice Two examples have mean selected-token losses 1.0 (one target) and 3.0 (three targets). What is the combined selected-token mean? Worked answer Use target counts as weights: (1 × 1.0 + 3 × 3.0) / (1 + 3) = 10/4 = 2.5. Averaging the two example means equally would give 2.0 and misrepresent their different target counts. A simple inference demonstration can select the largest score from the last row, breaking ties towards the lowest token ID. UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderPredictNext exposes this raw ID prediction. UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderGenerateGreedy repeats it, shifting the context left between requested tokens. The current laboratory does not supply temperature sampling, a streaming chat protocol, tool-use permissions, an EOS stopping policy or verified natural-language capability. Greedy token IDs may include reserved special IDs. Never execute generated text as source code or financial instructions. Where work grows With context length C and generated length G, this implementation performs G complete forward passes. Each pass runs every Transformer layer. Unlike the earlier single-block KV-cache study, there is no qualified per-layer cache for the stacked model. The reference workload processes C × G token rows per layer, plus token embedding and final projection work. For example, three layers, context eight and five generated tokens give 3 × 8 × 5 = 120 layer-token evaluations. This is a simple work counter, not elapsed time or a claim about multiply-add count. The implementation does not claim a multi-layer KV-cache speedup. Why a cache needs more proof When the oldest token leaves the window, learned absolute position indices shift. The hidden representation in an upper Transformer layer may also depend on earlier context, even if RoPE were later used. Preserving cached keys/values without proving the new context semantics risks changing model outputs. Practice What is the layer-token forward-work count for four layers, context length 12 and seven generated tokens? Worked answer 4 × 12 × 7 = 336 layer-token evaluations. It is not an actual runtime measurement. Benchmark with the same model, prompt, toolchain, warm-up and sampling semantics before discussing performance. A trustworthy training report should distinguish capacity evidence (which shapes and bytes fit), numerical evidence (whether logits, gradients and training steps are correct), and quality evidence (whether a model performs better on independent, authorised held-out cases). Learning objective: Follow the model's original fixed-context contract rather than changing its weights to make an application work. 1. Understand the engineering problem The previous course created a separately identified stacked decoder with multiple pre-layer-normalised Transformer blocks. Inference is the read-only part of its lifecycle. Inputs are numerical token IDs; the decoder uses embeddings, positional embeddings, successive attention/MLP blocks and a vocabulary projection to produce one logit per candidate token. No new training step is necessary to ask the model for a prediction. That separation matters: an application should never change model weights merely because a user asks a question. 2. Follow a concrete example Suppose the model has a context of four tokens, vocabulary size 260 and two Transformer layers. One call to UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderLogits receives exactly four token IDs and produces a row-major [4,260] float array: 1,040 logits. Only the fourth row is used to choose the immediate next token. Repeating the operation after appending an output produces another full [4,260] result. Four decoded positions times two layers gives eight logical token-layer rows per prediction, not eight GPU operations. 3. Implement through the Framework Use the new UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerationSessionCreate, ...Next and ...Destroy interfaces from umicom/ai/training/stacked_inference.h. They call the existing stacked decoder for actual logits and reuse the Framework's nucleus sampler. The session borrows the model; it never becomes an alternative owner of attention, tensor memory or optimisers. Its public output is one ID at a time. Alternatively, UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerateNucleus stages a fixed number of IDs and publishes them together. 4. Check the boundaries This is a bounded experimental system: at most 64 output tokens per session. Its complete context is evaluated on every pull; no multi-layer KV cache has been introduced. Reproducible numeric tokens are not evidence that a model understands a language or can safely produce executable financial-system code. Display model identity, sampling policy and limited test scope in any educational viewer. Practice Question: If a four-token model has three stacked Transformer layers, how many layer-token rows are evaluated for five generated tokens? Reveal the worked answer Each pull calculates four rows through each of three layers: 4 × 3 = 12. Five pulls therefore request 5 × 12 = 60 layer-token rows. This is an accounting unit, not measured elapsed time. Continue Return to the native stacked inference learning path. For the mathematical background, read the stacked inference mathematics guide. Learning objective: Explain how short prompts and longer histories occupy learned absolute positions. 1. Understand the engineering problem A decoder with learned absolute positional embeddings does not treat a token at position zero as the same numerical input as that token at position three. Its position vector is added before the first Transformer layer. Consequently prompt layout is a semantic decision, not a cosmetic memory-copy detail. The stacked generation interface deliberately retains the older full-context, beginning-of-sequence (BOS) left-padding rule. 2. Follow a concrete example With context length four and the two byte tokens for in, the numeric prompt is [109,114]. The complete input becomes [BOS,BOS,109,114], where BOS is reserved ID 1. The model predicts using logits from index 3. After it emits token x, the next context becomes [BOS,109,114,x]. After the next emission y, it becomes [109,114,x,y]. When another token arrives, the oldest ID falls out, the three surviving IDs shift left and their learned positions change. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerationSessionCreate validates every supplied ID before constructing the retained context. Even if a prompt has more than four tokens, an invalid older ID is rejected rather than ignored. A permitted prompt can contain up to 4,096 IDs; only its latest context-length entries are retained. The session copies the retained context. Applications need not preserve the original prompt array after successful creation. 4. Check the boundaries Because a rolling context changes the input positions, retaining upper-layer hidden states without a new proof could give different logits. The existing single-block rotary research does not establish correct multi-layer eviction semantics. This implementation intentionally recomputes the entire stack rather than inventing a cache speedup. Use the distinct unpadded-prefix teaching API only when its different semantics are explicitly intended. Practice Question: For a five-position context and a three-token prompt, how many BOS tokens precede the prompt? Reveal the worked answer Two BOS tokens are inserted on the left: 5 − 3 = 2. The three real prompt IDs occupy positions 2, 3 and 4. Continue Return to the native stacked inference learning path. For the mathematical background, read the stacked inference mathematics guide. Learning objective: Learn how logits become reproducible decisions without inventing another sampler. 1. Understand the engineering problem The decoder produces real-valued scores called logits. Their ordering identifies which IDs the model currently favours, but a score is not itself a probability. Umicom Framework already provides a temperature-aware top-K and top-p (nucleus) sampler. A stacked model needs to call that established owner instead of implementing a second softmax, random-number generator or selection rule in the application. 2. Follow a concrete example Imagine candidate scores of 3, 2 and 1. At temperature one, softmax weights are approximately 0.665, 0.245, 0.090. Top-K equal to two initially discards the third candidate. Within the remaining two candidates, top-p of 0.8 retains the smallest ranked prefix whose cumulative normalised mass reaches 0.8. The first candidate has mass around 0.731 after top-K filtering, so the nucleus includes both. Exactly which ID is sampled still depends on the seeded random draw. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingNucleusOptions supplies temperature, topK and topP. Create a UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerationSession using one numeric seed and reuse the session for successive pulls. The existing UmiAiTrainingSampleLogitsNucleus receives the final-row logits and the allowed range [4,vocabularySize). topK=1 chooses the best allowed ID deterministically with no random draw; for larger choices the Framework RNG is advanced only after a successful selection. 4. Check the boundaries Sampling deliberately excludes reserved PAD/BOS/EOS/UNK IDs 0–3, even though the model's raw logits include those positions and supervised loss may target EOS. Thus output does not stop automatically at EOS. A zero probability, a malformed temperature or a top-K limit outside the allowed range is a rejected configuration, not grounds for silently substituting a default policy. The chosen policy belongs in reproducibility evidence. Practice Question: Can the same model and seed give a different stream when top-p changes? Reveal the worked answer Yes. Top-p changes the set of candidates before a random draw, so the selection distribution may change. Compare streams only when model checkpoint, prompt, seed and all sampler options match. Learning objective: Implement incremental user-visible delivery without claiming faster arithmetic. 1. Understand the engineering problem Streaming describes when the caller receives output: one token at a time rather than after a whole response. It is not the same as incremental attention computation. The stacked decoder currently has a correct canonical full-context path, while multi-layer cache equivalence after eviction remains unproved. The new session therefore provides a real streaming interface while still recomputing all layers for each token. 2. Follow a concrete example Suppose a model has context four, two layers and the user requests six output tokens. The session performs six complete inference calls. The logical work counters are 4 × 6 = 24 full-context token rows and 24 × 2 = 48 Transformer token-layer rows. These numbers come from the model shape and successful pull count. They do not include matrix dimensions, softmax work, allocation overhead, clock time or operating-system scheduling. A GUI may still feel more responsive because the first token arrives before the sixth. 3. Implement through the Framework A caller initialises a session pointer to NULL, invokes UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerationSessionCreate, repeatedly calls UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerationSessionNext, and finally destroys the session. Successful pulls increment its output counter and roll the retained context. An invalid call does not advance the random generator or replace the caller's token variable. Inspect reports the genuine count of successful pulls, alongside calculated work units and pinned checkpoint identity. 4. Check the boundaries Destroying the session is an explicit cancellation operation. It frees its own context and RNG state without destroying the borrowed decoder. No background worker or automatic restart is introduced. A real application must serialise decoder calls and must keep the decoder alive until the session is destroyed. This educational API emits at most 64 tokens; longer tasks need separately designed resource and lifetime policies. Practice Question: A six-token run reports 48 layer-token rows. Does this establish 48 floating-point operations or a particular latency? Reveal the worked answer No. A token-layer row stands for processing one token through one Transformer block. Each block may perform many matrix and attention operations; timings must be measured separately. Continue Return to the native stacked inference learning path. Learning objective: Use the existing reversible tokenizer without treating binary output as text. 1. Understand the engineering problem The native byte tokenizer maps each byte value 0–255 to a numeric ID by adding four, leaving IDs 0–3 reserved for special symbols. This mapping is reversible. It also means a model can generate a raw byte that is not printable text. An application that inserts a NUL terminator or assumes every output byte is a complete UTF-8 character can silently lose data or display corrupted text. 2. Follow a concrete example Consider the input byte sequence [0, 67, 10, 255]. The tokenizer maps it to [4, 71, 14, 259]. Byte zero is ordinary source data here, not the reserved PAD token ID zero. After generation, any output token from 4 to 259 can be mapped back to a byte by subtracting four. A four-byte UTF-8 character may arrive across several generated tokens, so even individually valid output bytes need a streaming decoder or buffer before rendering. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerateBytesNucleus delegates tokenisation to UmiAiByteEncode, uses the same stacked token-generation service and decodes IDs through UmiAiByteDecode. It returns an explicit output byte count and does not add a string terminator. ...SessionNextByte exposes one raw byte for a vocabulary of exactly 260 IDs. Source and destination capacities are measured in bytes here, while the token API capacities are measured in size_t elements. 4. Check the boundaries Do not execute generated content, treat it as a command, or use it as a banking instruction. Malformed UTF-8 should be handled by a separate presentation layer rather than rewritten inside the tokenizer. When saving a candidate response, retain exact bytes and model identity for repeatable evaluation; never confuse a display conversion with the original model output. Practice Question: What token ID represents a byte with numerical value 255? Reveal the worked answer The tokenizer adds four: 255 + 4 = 259. The inverse decoder subtracts four to recover 255. The reserved token ID 3 does not represent byte value 3. Continue Return to the native stacked inference learning path. For the mathematical background, read the stacked inference mathematics guide. Learning objective: Distinguish model-content integrity from publisher authentication. 1. Understand the engineering problem A decoder may keep the same configuration after its weights have changed. For instance, two models can each have vocabulary 260, context four and two layers, but different trained parameters. Checking dimensions alone does not identify a model. The Framework's stacked checkpoint encoder already supplies a canonical portable byte representation, which provides a suitable input for exact content identity. 2. Follow a concrete example Imagine opening an assistant session and then training the borrowed model before requesting its next token. Its step count and checkpoint bytes can change. The session's original prompt, seed and sampling policy would now refer to a different numerical function. The new identity component captures model configuration, completed training steps, checkpoint length and SHA-256 of the actual encoded bytes. Verify repeats that capture and refuses stale sessions. This is more precise than comparing a pointer or model name. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedModelIdentityCapture and ...Verify are Framework-owned APIs. The generation session uses them at creation, before sampling and before publishing a result. The model remains borrowed; the session does not copy the model's entire weights for separate inference. Every failed identity check leaves the caller's token/output record untouched. In particular, a model with the same tensor shapes but a different training seed does not silently pass. 4. Check the boundaries SHA-256 is an unkeyed content digest. Anyone who controls both a model and its claimed digest can make them match. Authenticating a publisher, approving usage rights and validating signed release evidence remain distinct Framework security duties. Do not present an identity match as a trusted financial-model deployment decision. Practice Question: If two checkpoints have the same layer count and vocabulary size, must they have the same SHA-256? Reveal the worked answer No. The digest covers exact encoded checkpoint bytes, including weight values and training state. Equal shapes are compatible dimensions, not identical model contents. Learning objective: Design sessions that remain valid across user-interface interactions and failures. 1. Understand the engineering problem An application may display one token, receive a cancel request, or change projects while an AI assistant is generating. Session lifetime must therefore be explicit. In native C23, ownership cannot be left to a scripting garbage collector. The Framework separates the caller-owned model from the session-owned context, sampler policy, random state and generation count. 2. Follow a concrete example Suppose the user cancels after three successful pulls. A session that has a four-token context and two layers has requested 12 full-context rows and 24 token-layer rows. Destroying the session releases its own state. It does not undo the three tokens already displayed, change model weights or create a background task. A subsequent request constructs a fresh session with its own seed and context. An attempted 65th pull after 64 successes is rejected without consuming a random number. 3. Implement through the Framework Use Create only with an output pointer initialised to NULL. Use Next only while the borrowed decoder is alive and not being trained concurrently. Check each returned UmiStatus before reading a token. Inspect can obtain the number of successful pulls; it refuses a model that no longer matches its captured checkpoint. Destroy accepts NULL, simplifying cleanup after partial construction in application code. 4. Check the boundaries A GUI adapter may request cancellation, but that does not make the decoding call itself interruptible mid-computation. The current synchronous boundary checks between tokens, not within every matrix multiplication. Future asynchronous scheduling should compose approved Framework task and cancellation services; it must not copy inference or RNG logic into the application. Practice Question: Who owns the decoder if a session is destroyed after a user cancels generation? Reveal the worked answer The application still owns the decoder. Destroying the session releases only session-owned context and random state; the caller must destroy the model separately when no user needs it. ← PreviousNext →Continuation catalogueCourse home Bits to Banking · Umicom Foundation Author: Sammy Hegab Topic: Native C23 Transformers, inference and independent validation. Learning objective: Check the complete decoder and sampler, not only a second copy of session state. 1. Understand the engineering problem Two session implementations can agree while sharing the same mistake. Stronger evidence reconstructs a separate canonical reference: build the documented BOS-left-padded context, run the established UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderLogits operation, sample from its last row with the same Framework nucleus sampler, then roll the context. This test is independent of the production session's orchestration. It is kept inside the test suite rather than shipped as a competing inference engine. 2. Follow a concrete example For context [BOS,BOS,109,114], a four-position model returns a [4,260] logit table. The reference reads entries 780–1039, because the last row starts at 3 × 260 = 780. After the reference sampler chooses ID k, it rolls to [BOS,109,114,k]. Repeating the calculation six times yields a reference sequence. A production session started with the same seed, prompt and policy must return every ID in the same order. 3. Implement through the Framework The new test_stacked_inference_reference.c exercises both deterministic top-K=1 and seeded nucleus sampling. It also checks outputs after the context is full and older tokens are evicted. Comparing only the final token would miss an earlier divergence; comparing only row-count estimates would not prove numeric parity. Both checks should accompany checkpoint-identity and failure-atomic output tests. 4. Check the boundaries Do not compare against the separate unpadded-prefix generator: its prompt positions differ. Nor does a successful test prove that a future multi-layer KV cache is equivalent. A cache optimisation requires independent attention-logit comparisons across every layer and position, especially after eviction. The reference deliberately recomputes the whole context. Practice Question: Why must the reference read the last real position's logits rather than an arbitrary row? Reveal the worked answer The next token is predicted from the final position in the current complete input context. Earlier rows predict from earlier prefixes and can have different causal histories. Learning objective: Separate logical token-layer work from elapsed time and memory traffic. 1. Understand the engineering problem When discussing performance, engineers often use different denominators without noticing. Token count, token-layer rows, matrix multiply–accumulates, process CPU time, wall-clock duration and peak memory are different quantities. The new stacked session exposes an intentionally narrow workload counter: the number of full-context token rows requested and the same number multiplied by Transformer layer count. 2. Follow a concrete example With context length eight, three layers and ten generated tokens, the session requests 8 × 10 = 80 complete-context token rows. It also requests 80 × 3 = 240 layer-token rows. This says nothing directly about the work of attention softmax, the C×C projections, per-layer feed-forward widths, or token-embedding lookup. A model with twice as many channels can do much more arithmetic while keeping the same row counters. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerationSessionInspect derives counts from the model configuration and successful calls. They are deterministic and suitable for checking whether a session performed the expected amount of work. They are not measurements of CPU instructions or seconds. For genuine comparisons, use a qualified benchmark with equal model, prompt, compiler settings, sampling seed and workload, then record warm-up, repetitions and variability separately. 4. Check the boundaries Multi-layer KV caching is especially delicate. A retained upper-layer key may depend on hidden states that already incorporated evicted tokens. RoPE alone does not guarantee a new rolling-window reference would compute the same value. Never advertise throughput gains from a proposed cache until numerical invariants and timings have both been demonstrated. Practice Question: A context-four, layer-five model emits seven tokens. How many token-layer rows are requested? Reveal the worked answer It requests 4 × 7 × 5 = 140 token-layer rows. That is distinct from the 28 full-context rows and is not an elapsed-time measurement. Learning objective: Combine read-only losses by supervised target count rather than by document count. 1. Understand the engineering problem Training examples can contain different numbers of assistant-response tokens. If their loss masks select different numbers of targets, averaging one mean loss per example gives the wrong aggregate. The desired quantity is mean cross-entropy per selected token. The stacked decoder already provides selected-token evaluation through the training tape, so the new evaluator reuses that owner rather than implementing a competing softmax. 2. Follow a concrete example Example A supervises one target and has mean loss 0.2. Example B supervises three targets and has mean loss 0.8. The correct combined average is (1 × 0.2 + 3 × 0.8) / (1 + 3) = 2.6 / 4 = 0.65. Simply averaging (0.2+0.8)/2 = 0.5 falsely treats the one-token example as equally influential as the three-token example. Both examples must use the same model, and each must be held out from training. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedEvaluationRun accepts a bounded collection of UmiAiTrainingStackedEvaluationCase values. Each case contains token IDs, targets, a binary loss mask, the fixed context length and a caller-supplied original-source digest. The service validates mask values and only requires target IDs at selected positions to be valid. It calls UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderEvaluateSelected for each example and calculates the weighted aggregate in double precision. 4. Check the boundaries This service cannot determine whether a dataset was legally obtained, accurately transcribed, properly redacted or genuinely unseen during training. Use existing source-admission and reviewed-corpus controls before constructing evaluation windows. The SHA-256 returned for the ordered cases identifies supplied bytes but is not a licence certificate or signature. Practice Question: If two examples select two and six tokens respectively, which example contributes more to token-weighted mean loss? Reveal the worked answer The six-target example contributes three times as much weight as the two-target example. Each target counts once; the document count does not determine the denominator. Learning objective: Score exact next-token predictions using the same verified logits as evaluation loss. 1. Understand the engineering problem Cross-entropy considers how much probability the model assigns to the correct target. Top-one accuracy asks a different question: for each supervised position, does the single highest-scoring vocabulary ID equal the target ID? It is possible to have a better cross-entropy without changing the top prediction, or to change top-one accuracy while the average loss changes only slightly. 2. Follow a concrete example Suppose the loss mask for a four-position sequence is [0,1,1,0]. Only positions 1 and 2 count. At position 1, the model's highest logit belongs to ID 45 and the target is 45: one match. At position 2, the model favours ID 80 while the target is 81: a miss. The top-one accuracy is 1 / 2 = 0.5, or 50%. The ignored positions contribute neither matches nor misses, even if their unmasked logits are confidently wrong. 3. Implement through the Framework The evaluator calls the established UmiAiTrainingStackedDecoderLogits and scans the vocabulary only for selected rows. Equal logits break ties toward the lower ID, consistent with the model's greedy convention. A non-finite inspected logit is an invalid numerical state rather than a guess. The report includes selected target count, match count and the resulting fraction. It does not sample random tokens to measure top-one predictions. 4. Check the boundaries The complete training loss can include EOS as a supervised target, even though the generation sampler excludes the four reserved IDs. Keep these two policies distinct. A high top-one score on a tiny reviewed dataset does not demonstrate that the model writes correct source code, answers customer questions reliably or follows security boundaries. Practice Question: What accuracy results from three exact predictions among five selected targets? Reveal the worked answer The fraction is 3 / 5 = 0.6, or 60%. Ignored rows are not added to the denominator. Continue Return to the native stacked inference learning path. For the mathematical background, read the stacked inference mathematics guide. Learning objective: Convert average next-token cross-entropy into a useful but limited diagnostic. 1. Understand the engineering problem Perplexity is a conventional way to express the uncertainty represented by average next-token cross-entropy. For losses measured using natural logarithms, perplexity equals the exponential of mean loss. It is often convenient for comparing models on an identical tokenisation scheme and held-out data, but it is not a direct percentage accuracy or a human-quality rating. 2. Follow a concrete example If selected-token cross-entropy is ln(2) ≈ 0.6931, perplexity is exp(0.6931) ≈ 2. If loss is ln(4) ≈ 1.3863, perplexity is about 4. Smaller perplexity is usually preferable for the same measured next-token task. But evaluating one model with byte tokens and another with subword tokens changes the prediction units, so their raw perplexities are not automatically comparable. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedEvaluationRun first obtains a genuine token-weighted loss from the canonical decoder, then computes its exponential. If the result is too large to represent as a finite double, the report leaves perplexity at zero and sets perplexityAvailable=0. Zero in that case is not a magical perfect model: it is an explicit unavailable-value marker. The original loss and other metrics remain available. 4. Check the boundaries Perplexity does not measure truthfulness, instruction-following, privacy protection, toxicity, software reliability or financial accuracy. Keep additional independently reviewed evaluation suites and safety checks before promoting a model. Do not tune a model solely to reduce one held-out metric after repeatedly inspecting that same held-out set; that can also cause evaluation contamination. Practice Question: If natural-log cross-entropy is exactly zero, what mathematical perplexity follows? Reveal the worked answer exp(0) = 1. This is the mathematical minimum for an idealised correct-token probability of one; it is not a realistic claim of general intelligence. Continue Return to the native stacked inference learning path. Learning objective: Separate numerical acceptance criteria from actual release authorisation. 1. Understand the engineering problem A fine-tuned candidate should be compared with its reference model using exactly the same held-out cases and context rules. Comparing different prompt lengths, tokenisations, source partitions or model shapes can manufacture an apparent improvement. The new Framework selection service evaluates both stacked models using the same evaluator and verifies that their declared decoder dimensions are compatible. 2. Follow a concrete example Suppose reference loss is 0.80 and candidate loss is 0.83. If the policy allows an absolute loss increase of at most 0.02, the candidate fails the loss condition because 0.83 − 0.80 = 0.03. If the candidate has top-one accuracy 0.62 and the policy requires at least 0.60, its accuracy condition passes. Overall admission still fails because both conditions must pass. This is an evaluation result, not a software error. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedModelSelectionCompare accepts a reference model, candidate model, one held-out case array and an explicit policy. It checks matching shape, runs read-only evaluation for both and returns separate lossAccepted, accuracyAccepted and candidateAccepted fields. Invalid policies—such as negative loss tolerance or accuracy greater than one—are rejected without overwriting the caller's report. A failed numerical threshold returns status OK with candidateAccepted=0. 4. Check the boundaries The service is deliberately not an autonomous deployment gate. It does not approve a signing key, grant model execution permissions or decide whether the model may place trades or payments. Framework security and explicit human review remain separate. Use independent quality criteria for generated code, model hallucinations, privacy and appropriate domain behaviour. Practice Question: When accuracy passes but maximum allowed loss regression fails, should the candidate be accepted? Reveal the worked answer No. The comparison requires both threshold conditions to pass. A valid rejected candidate is represented with candidateAccepted=0 and a successful API status. Learning objective: Bind output IDs to the exact checkpoint, prompt, sampler policy and seed. 1. Understand the engineering problem A transcript without model identity is difficult to reproduce. Even identical text may have been generated using different weights or prompt positions. The native Framework's stacked evidence API makes reproducibility an explicit test: it receives claimed output token IDs, regenerates them using the canonical session, compares every ID, and only then publishes aggregate identifiers. 2. Follow a concrete example Consider a prompt with two IDs and a run of six generated IDs. The evidence record contains the prompt-token count, output-token count, sampler temperature, top-K/top-p, initial RNG seed and model checkpoint identity. It also contains independent SHA-256 digests for ordered prompt IDs, ordered output IDs and the sampling declaration. Token IDs are encoded as fixed-width little-endian numbers before hashing so the identity does not depend on whether a host uses 32-bit or 64-bit size_t. The record contains no raw prompt text. 3. Implement through the Framework UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerationEvidenceBuild recomputes the entire output. If even one claimed token differs from the regenerated token, the call returns an invalid-state result without publishing a report. ...EvidenceVerify repeats the check using the stored policy and seed and compares the digests and model work fields. These APIs never compile, execute or trust generated code; they do not write files or contact an external model. 4. Check the boundaries Unkeyed hashes are not digital signatures. A malicious party who can replace a checkpoint, output and evidence can compute matching new digests. Reproducibility does not establish ethical training-data sourcing, copyright permission, model safety or organisational approval. Those claims require other evidence and controls. Practice Question: If a replay generates five matching IDs and a different sixth ID, should evidence for all six be published? Learning objective: Keep caller buffers and model state unchanged after invalid requests. 1. Understand the engineering problem A robust native library must refuse malformed requests without leaving half-written outputs or advancing generation state. That property is called failure atomicity. It matters in AI systems just as it matters in banking software: incomplete data must never masquerade as a complete and approved result. An unsafe code path can appear to work in happy-path demonstrations while failing when capacities or identities change. 2. Follow a concrete example Imagine a caller requests three tokens but supplies capacity for only two. UmiAiTrainingStackedGenerateNucleus must reject the request before writing the token array, output count or optional statistics. If a prompt includes token 999 while the vocabulary has only 260 entries, Create must refuse the entire prompt—even if the offending token would have fallen outside the retained four-position context. If a borrowed model has been trained since a session started, later pulls must refuse its stale checkpoint identity. 3. Implement through the Framework The tests cover invalid top-p values, invalid output count, null pointers, insufficient capacity, malformed loss masks, missing supervised targets, wrong model shape, changed checkpoint digests and stale sessions. Separate execution tests check reproducibility. The Framework's model and arrays remain caller-owned according to their documented lifetime contracts, while sessions and temporary logits are owned by the relevant Framework services. 4. Check the boundaries Passing these tests is not a guarantee that C23 code contains no memory defect. Repeat under native Windows UCRT64 and compatible Linux builds; use AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviourSanitizer where appropriate.
